reason: B offers the more physically plausible and directly testable mechanism: annealing-induced Cu-rich phase separation is credible in FeNiCrCoCu and can be verified before correlating precipitates with deformation and wear. A relies on the poorly supported claim that high-temperature dislocation climb promotes twinning within the coating—where climb more commonly relaxes stresses—and its cited evidence concerns twinning in a nickel substrate at 300 K, not high-temperature sliding.
